title: Network Effects
hook: The best products get better every time someone new joins. Most products don't.
statement: With a network effect, every new user makes the product more valuable for everyone else.
explainer: That's one of the strongest moats there is. Once people stay because other people are there, leaving means losing the network, not just switching tools.
sop: Name what a new user adds for everyone else: content, connections, data.
Ask if the product is truly worse with 10 Users than with 1,000.
Build one feature that shows other users' activity to new ones.
Count your active Users and rate how much each new one adds, 1 to 10.
Protect early users' experience while you chase growth.
equation_example: Value grows roughly with Users squared. 10 users: 10 × 10 = 100. 100 users: 100 × 100 = 10,000. Growing faster than a straight line means a real network effect. A straight line means you just have more users.
question: Write down what one new user gives every other user in your product. If it's nothing, write that.
closing_statement: Design for what users give each other, not you.
caption:
Principle Nº 174: Network Effects

The best products get better every time someone new joins. Most products don't.

With a network effect, every new user makes the product more valuable for everyone else.
